findings: Fetal umbilical vessels lead to capillaries within villi; maternal vessels open to blood spaces outside the fetal capillaries.
Inset distinguishes fetal and maternal portions and shows their boundary; no direct merged maternal/fetal blood tube is drawn.
Labels for uterus, placenta, cord and amniotic fluid are readable at native extraction size.
Use an authored equivalent to explain directional names: umbilical arteries carry blood away from the fetus; the umbilical vein carries blood toward it.
Colour is illustrative and cannot replace direction labels. This is a section through a complex branching interface, not a complete vessel count or to-scale reconstruction.
Original caption oversimplifies all nutrient transfer as diffusion; it is excluded. Adjacent teaching must distinguish gas diffusion from other selective transport processes.

alt: Section of a placenta showing maternal blood around branching villi and fetal capillaries inside them, connected to the umbilical vessels.
equivalent: Chorionic villi are branching projections of placental tissue. Fetal capillaries are small blood vessels inside these projections; maternal blood occupies spaces around them. Tissue separates the two blood supplies.

Umbilical arteries carry fetal blood to the placenta. The umbilical vein returns blood toward the fetus. Oxygen commonly moves toward fetal blood and carbon dioxide toward maternal blood; other substances use different selective transfer processes.
Blood-vessel direction and the exchange boundary matter more than red or blue colouring. The placenta is not an absolute filter against harmful exposures.
